season.evidence: Stored Jul-Sep. Web search found no page that dates this specific line; north-side snow lingers early (heavy early-season snow makes the north face intimidating), July and September reports found it snow-free; histogram peaks Jul-Sep.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Oct 3 report only says to finish on the NE side of the summit block, which is the standard Windy Pass finish; nothing names a traverse to a low point on the NE ridge. Also one month past window.
Oct 24, unnamed route, no NE ridge description; offseason.

season.evidence: Search: a trip report calls the SE route a good early-season option since it melts out first; an aggregator says late spring through mid summer; logged SE-route ascents fall in Jul (3), Sep, and one early Oct. Kept May-Sep, Oct tolerated as +1 month.

track.why: Logged route "SE Approach"; July 15 report describes the old jeep road, burned hillside, a meadow near 5,700 ft and the gully toward the saddle, matching our SE Route text; track leaves the Eightmile trail early and climbs the SE slopes directly (not via Windy Pass); summited; round trip from our trailhead pin (start 74 m, end 53 m).

otherTracksConsidered.why: Oct 8 2022 "SE Gulley", same line, summited, complete; one month past the window so second choice.
Unnamed, Oct 24, reaches the summit via the maintained trail.

facts.text: In mid-July the burned slope above the old road is overgrown with thick, leafy brush over loose ash; the first hour is slow.

The old jeep road is hard to keep to under regrowth; one party found the going easier after climbing straight up to a meadow near 5,700 ft, then angling across at a gentler pitch to about 7,200 ft below the saddle.
In early October the gully line has no boot-pack at all, so expect to route-find alone; the final scramble is longer and more solid than the standard finish.

notes: West Ridge already has a track and is not in this packet. 3367730 and 3388399 (Oct) are standard Windy Pass ascents. NE Ridge: no harvested track names it. Both SE-route tracks come down the standard (west) side, so only the ascent follows the SE line.
